channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened Against Kyrgyz Students for Insulting Kazakh Ancestors
item.description: Kazakh authorities have launched a pre-trial investigation against two female students from Kyrgyzstan for allegedly making offensive remarks about the skull of Khan Kenesary. An attorney confirmed the criminal case registration after filing a complaint. The students had posted videos containing insults directed at Kazakh ancestors, the country, and the nation, despite having issued apologies.

item.title: Significance of Iranian President's Appearance at CIS Summit Revealed
item.description: The presence of the Iranian President at the jubilee summit of CIS heads of state carries significant geopolitical implications. The article explores the potential reasons and consequences of this participation, analyzing its impact on regional dynamics and international relations within the Commonwealth of Independent States framework.

item.title: Kazakhstan woman convicted for fake sick leave appeals to Constitutional Court
item.description: A woman in Kazakhstan, convicted for using a forged sick leave note, challenged the legality of evidence seizure. She argued police confiscated her medical documents without a judge's warrant, violating privacy. The Constitutional Court ruled that determining if a document contains protected information and if a warrant was needed is case-specific and up to the trial court.

item.title: New Tashkent to allocate 100 hectares each to all regions and capital districts
item.description: New Tashkent will allocate 100 hectares of land to each region and district of the capital. Regional entrepreneurs will be able to implement investment projects on these allocated lands. Participation in the initial auction for land plots will be limited to entrepreneurs from the respective region.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ride-Sharing and Delivery Services Face Disruptions, Users Seek Alternatives
item.description: Ride-sharing and delivery services within Yandex Go in Kazakhstan experienced disruptions over the weekend, prompting users to discuss alternatives on social media. While Yandex Go confirmed technical issues, users speculated about drone attacks on Yandex infrastructure. Other services like Dodo Pizza were also affected. Users are exploring various local ride-sharing platforms, some operating on a peer-to-peer model.

item.title: Riyadh Airport Attacked Again: One Dead, 11 Injured in Latest Incident
item.description: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport was attacked again on October 11, resulting in one death and 11 injuries, according to Associated Press and Reuters. Saudi-led coalition forces reported an unidentified projectile hit passenger Terminal 4, causing a fire. This marks the fourth attack on the airport in a week amid the coalition's offensive against Houthis in Yemen. The airport remains closed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor Offers 45 Services Online, 28 Proactively
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection announced that 45 out of 49 services are now available online, with 28 offered proactively. Citizens can access these services through the e-government portal, the Enbek.kz labor exchange, mobile apps, and second-tier bank applications, reducing the need for in-person visits.

item.title: Tajikistan Court Hears Case of Husband Accused of Driving Wife to Suicide
item.description: A court in Tajikistan has begun proceedings in the case of Mohitobon Ahmadova, 21, who died in May. Her family claims she was beaten to death, while her husband's family says she committed suicide. The prosecution accuses the husband, Muhammadzubayr Abdulfaizov, of driving her to suicide and seeks an eight-year prison sentence.

item.title: Contraband Chinese trucks worth 605 million tenge sold via state procurement
item.description: Three individuals were convicted in Astana for illegally importing 20 Chinese FAW trucks into Kazakhstan between February and May 2023. The trucks, declared as 'Euro-5' but actually 'Euro-2', had a customs value of 285 million tenge and were later sold for 605 million tenge through commercial structures and state procurement to 'QAZJolServis'.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Exempt Investors from Green Space Requirements in New Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan will cancel the requirement for investors to allocate 30% of land for green spaces in New Tashkent. The state will ensure 30% green coverage for the city based on the master plan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced this at a meeting with investors and entrepreneurs. Costs for "green" certificates for non-residential projects exceeding $50 million will be fully covered by the state.

item.title: Flash Floods Possible in Several Regions of Uzbekistan on October 13-14
item.description: Flash floods may occur in foothill and mountainous areas of Uzbekistan on October 13-14 due to rainfall, according to Uzhydromet. Affected regions include parts of Kashkadarya, Surkhandarya, Samarkand, Navoi, Jizzakh, Tashkent, Namangan, Fergana, and Andijan provinces. Residents and drivers in these areas are advised to take precautions.

item.title: American Entrepreneur Invites Global Crypto Investors to Invest in Alatau City Project
item.description: American entrepreneur and investor Balaji Srinivasan urged international crypto investors to fund the Alatau City project, highlighting Astana's potential as a tech and investment hub. Speaking at The Network State Conference in Singapore, Srinivasan described Kazakhstan's capital as a beautiful and well-maintained city. He also announced plans for his Network School project to relocate to Kazakhstan, with a five-year memorandum signed for a new campus and annual conferences.

item.title: Kazakhstan Lags in Copper Processing Despite New Deposits Due to Lack of New Smelting Plants
item.description: Kazakhstan faces a challenge in copper processing, needing to develop processing capabilities alongside extraction to retain added value domestically. While new deposits are being explored, such as Karatas, and existing plants like Balkhash (producing 51% of the country's cathode copper) are being modernized, the construction of new smelting plants is lagging. The government is considering new regulations, including tariffs and export duties, to link the growing raw material base with domestic processing.

item.title: Kazakh President Consults on Early Termination of Local Assembly Elections
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held consultations with the Prime Minister and the Chairman of the Kurultai regarding the early termination of the powers of local assemblies (maslikhats) at all levels. The President emphasized the importance of maslikhats for citizens' interests, budget approval, and regional development. He expressed confidence that renewing the deputy corps would strengthen local representative bodies. A final decision will be made in accordance with the Constitution.

item.title: Kazakhstan Recovers Billions of Tenge from Victims of Online Fraud
item.description: Over eight months this year, 5.9 billion tenge has been reimbursed to victims of online fraud in Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported a 40% decrease in cybercrime cases over three years, with over a thousand individuals prosecuted. The National Bank's Anti-Fraud Center blocked suspicious operations exceeding 117 billion tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Early Termination of Local Assemblies' Mandates
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan is considering the early termination of the mandates of local representative bodies (maslikhats) at all levels. Consultations were held with the Prime Minister and the Chairman of the Kurultai. The head of state expressed confidence that renewing the deputy corps would strengthen the work of these bodies.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Airport Kills One, Injures Eleven
item.description: A Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resulted in one death and eleven injuries, according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation. A Pakistani national was killed, and material damage occurred. A previous attack on Saturday reportedly caused at least 12 deaths and over 300 injuries.

item.title: New Tashkent Infrastructure Fee Base Rate to be Reduced Up to 10 Times
item.description: Infrastructure fees in New Tashkent will be revised to stimulate the construction of service and social facilities. The base rate for commercial, service, and business centers will be reduced threefold, for hotels and tourism facilities fivefold, and for cultural and entertainment venues tenfold. Fees for private kindergartens, schools, and hospitals will be set at 1%.

item.title: Serik Kenzhebayev Appointed Head of Apparatus at Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
item.description: Serik Kenzhebayev has been appointed to the position of Head of the Apparatus at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan. This appointment signifies a key role within the ministry's administrative structure.

item.title: Lenovo and QAIRU Launch AI Classroom to Advance Artificial Intelligence in Education
item.description: Lenovo and QAIRU have opened an AI classroom, a joint educational and research platform for developing and applying artificial intelligence technologies in education. Established on the initiative of Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Qazaq AI Research University aims to foster AI development and train specialists in machine learning and data analysis. The Lenovo AI Class will serve as a practical laboratory for learning and implementing advanced AI technologies.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Means-Test Childbirth and Disability Benefits from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will implement a new policy restricting access to several state benefits, including childbirth and disability payments. The government's revised approach, outlined in Resolution No. 870, will make eligibility dependent on a family's financial situation, shifting from universal support to a targeted system. This change affects ten types of benefits previously guaranteed regardless of income.

item.title: Riyadh Airport Attacked Again: One Dead, 11 Injured
item.description: Riyadh's international airport was attacked again, resulting in one death and 11 injuries, according to Associated Press and Reuters. Saudi-led coalition forces reported an unidentified projectile hit Terminal 4, causing a fire. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry condemned the attacks, calling them a violation of international law and detrimental to peace efforts in Yemen. This marks the fourth attack on Riyadh airport in a week.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Diversify Arms Purchases Beyond Russia
item.description: Tajikistan and Turkmenistan have received Akash surface-to-air missile systems from India, marking a shift away from reliance on Russian weaponry. While details remain undisclosed, these acquisitions offer an alternative to the Soviet and Russian systems that have historically dominated Central Asian arsenals. Experts suggest this move signals a political statement to Moscow regarding regional security autonomy.

item.title: Organizer of Drug Labs in Almaty Extradited from Russia to Kazakhstan
item.description: A Kazakhstani citizen, suspected of organizing a criminal group involved in the production and sale of psychotropic substances, has been extradited from Russia to Kazakhstan. The group allegedly operated drug laboratories in Almaty, where two individuals died from chemical poisoning. Authorities seized over 24 kg of chemicals and equipment.

item.title: Organizer of Deadly Drug Lab in Almaty Extradited from Russia
item.description: An individual suspected of organizing a criminal group that produced and distributed mephedrone has been extradited from Russia to Kazakhstan. The group allegedly operated several drug labs in Almaty, where two members died from chemical poisoning. Authorities seized over 24 kg of chemicals and equipment during a raid.

item.title: Kazakh President Consults on Early Termination of Local Council Powers
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held consultations with the Prime Minister and the Chairman of the Kurultai regarding the early termination of the powers of local councils (maslikhats). Tokayev emphasized the importance of their full functioning for ensuring citizens' legal interests and regional development. He believes renewing the deputy corps will strengthen local representative bodies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Relocate All Ministries and State Organizations to New Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to relocate all ministries and state organizations to the newly developing New Tashkent. Currently, the Ministries of Construction, Transport, and Energy are operational in the new city. The Prime Minister has been tasked with initiating the relocation process for other ministries and state entities.

item.title: Suspect in Drug Lab Organization Extradited from Russia to Kazakhstan
item.description: A suspect accused of organizing a mephedrone production lab in Almaty, which allegedly led to two deaths, has been extradited from Russia. The organized group, formed in 2021, produced and distributed psychotropic substances remotely managed via Telegram. Authorities seized over 24 kg of chemicals and equipment.

item.title: Turkey Urges Immediate Cessation of Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Turkey has condemned the Houthi attacks targeting Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and called for an immediate halt. The Turkish Foreign Ministry expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, stating the attacks violate international law and threaten regional security. Ankara reaffirmed support for Saudi Arabia's sovereignty.

item.title: Pakistan Deploys Military to Peshawar Amidst Emergency Rule and Protests
item.description: Pakistan has deployed military personnel and vehicles to Peshawar following the imposition of emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The move comes amid anti-government demonstrations by supporters of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan and increased militant violence. Authorities cited deteriorating security and failed negotiations as reasons for the emergency measures.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Discusses Early Termination of Maslikhats' Authority
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has discussed the issue of prematurely terminating the authority of maslikhats (local representative bodies). The discussion focused on the specific circumstances and procedures for such a termination, indicating potential reforms in local governance structures within Kazakhstan.

item.title: UN Agency Warns Thousands of Returnee Families Need Shelter as Winter Approaches
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warns that thousands of families returning to Afghanistan need urgent shelter, warmth, and protection as winter nears. Since the start of the year, over 1.29 million individuals have returned, many forcibly, from Pakistan and Iran. OCHA requires significant funding for humanitarian aid.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Orders Relocation of Ministries and State Organizations to New Tashkent
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed the Prime Minister to begin relocating remaining ministries and state organizations to New Tashkent, following the move of the Ministries of Construction, Transport, and Energy. The president emphasized the importance of this relocation for the city's business life during a meeting with investors and entrepreneurs on October 12.

item.title: Kazakhstan-born Russian Citizen on Hunger Strike in US Prison Deportation to Russia
item.description: A Russian citizen born in Kazakhstan, Idris Makhmudov, has been deported from the US to Russia. He was on hunger strike in a Georgia detention center protesting conditions and delays in his asylum case. His representative claims he was forcibly removed and lost consciousness.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Criticizes Bureaucracy Hindering Investment Projects in New Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that New Tashkent is not just a housing development area. He criticized bureaucratic obstacles hindering investment projects, emphasizing the need to review processes from land allocation to project launch. The president called for streamlining procedures for entrepreneurs.

item.title: OIC Envoy Pledges Continued Aid to Afghanistan in Humanitarian, Health, and Education Sectors
item.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation's special envoy for Afghanistan, Tariq Ali Bakheet, met with Taliban officials to emphasize the continuation of OIC assistance. Bakheet highlighted ongoing projects and stressed resolving regional issues through dialogue. The Taliban requested increased aid and attention to alternative livelihood programs to combat narcotics.

item.title: WFP Reports Afghan Laborers' Purchasing Power Down 25% Amidst Limited Work and High Food Prices
item.description: The World Food Programme reports that Afghan unskilled laborers' purchasing power has decreased by 25% compared to last year. Limited work opportunities, lower wages, and elevated food prices contribute to this decline. Workers are finding fewer days of work, and the cost of staple foods like rice, cooking oil, and wheat has significantly increased.

item.title: Uzbek President Calls for Review of Processes for Land Allocation and Project Launch in New Tashkent
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized the need to review processes from land allocation to project launch in New Tashkent. He stated the area should become an economic hub for business, education, and tourism, not just housing. The president noted that many allocated land plots have not seen construction, citing bureaucratic hurdles and a lack of investor support.

item.title: Over 1,500 CSTO Servicemembers Participate in 'Indestructible Brotherhood-2026' Exercises in Belarus
item.description: Over 1,500 military personnel are participating in the Collective Security Treaty Organization's (CSTO) command-staff exercises 'Indestructible Brotherhood-2026' and the special exercise 'Barrier-2026' in Belarus. The exercises focus on peacekeeping forces and joint radiation, chemical, biological protection, and medical support. The opening ceremony took place in Vitebsk.

item.title: Dushanbe Police Seize 386 Grams of Methamphetamine from Suspect
item.description: Dushanbe police arrested a 28-year-old national of a neighboring country on drug trafficking charges. Authorities seized 386 grams of crystal methamphetamine from the suspect during an operation. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the drugs were found both on his person and in his rented apartment. A criminal case has been initiated.
